code.description:
The problem code of its error (`SH1002`), or of its failure when
it ran and failed on the setup (`doctor`); `shuyi explain <code>`
prints its page.

error.description: Why it could not run, if it could not.

help.description: How to fix it, with the code.

limits.description: What it could not determine, in plain words.

ok.description:
Whether it passed: nothing found by a check, runs that agree, a
game made, a toolchain complete. False too when it could not run.

result.description: What it found or made; absent when it could not run.

backtrace.description: The backtrace as the standard library wrote it.

fatal.description: Whether the panic ended the game.

frames.description:
The frames of the panicking thread's stack, the innermost first:
named with `--symbols`, offsets without. Empty for a report from
macOS or the web, or one older than its frames.

game.description: The game's version, empty if the game gave none.

has_record.description:
Whether it holds the game's record of its play, for
`replay --crash`.

log.description: The log's last lines, oldest first.

target.description: The OS, the processor and the build: `linux x86_64 release`.

thread.description: The panicking thread's name, if it has one.

top_screen.description: The screen on top, if the game was running.

when.description: When it happened: milliseconds since 1970 on the game's clock.

NamedFrame.description:
A frame of a crash report's stack, the innermost first: where in the
program it was, and, from the debug file, the function, its file and
the line. An inlined function is a frame of its own, at the same
offset as the function it was inlined into.

file.description:
The function's source file, by the name the build gave it (a
release's paths remapped: `/cargo/registry/...`, the package's
name for the game's own).

function.description:
The function, as the debug file names it (its debug information,
or else its symbol table); `None` without `--symbols`, or where it
names none.

line.description: The line in `file`: of the call, for a frame that called another.

offset.description:
The return address minus the program's load address, as sixteen
hex digits; `None` for a frame in another module, such as a system
library.
